message1: %1 is defeated!
message2: %1 is slain!
message4: %1 is revived!
name: Dead
description:
Getting your rear end kicked in is no fun
when it happens in combat, or from
anything else that does you in.  Being
defeated means being dead - but not
forever, although it definitely means
being out for the count and unable to
fight in combat.  While a character is
defeated, they cannot participate in
combat, they cannot earn EXP
(Experience Points), and they have no
HP (Health Points) left.  Ordinary
healing potions and spells, as well as
resting at an Inn, won't work.  They need
special treatment and care to recover
from this condition (duh).
description2:
Many cities, towns, and villages have
priests and perhaps other people as well
who offer services that include brining
the dead back to life, for a small price.
\LB    Note that if all of the player
characters in the adventuring party are
dead at the same time, the game is over
and you lose the game.  When this
happens, hopefully you've saved your
progress at some point, so you can load a
saved game.  There isn't much else to say
about it, as this description has
probably already insulted your
intelligence if you have ever played
video games before and weren't born
yesterday.

message1: %1 guards, blocking and dodging attacks.
message2: %1 guards, blocking and dodging attacks.
message3: %1 guards, blocking and dodging attacks.
name: Guard
description:
Guarding is a special combat skill
available to all player characters in the
adventuring party.  When guarding, a
character's defense's are bolstered and
the damage they suffer if they are hit in
combat is reduced to half as much by
default, further modified by equipment
and gear as well as their natural ability
to avoid getting hurt and defend
themselves in combat.  Spells, items, and
certain equipment can change one's guard
effect.

message1: %1 temporarily cannot be killed.
message2: %1 temporarily cannot be killed.
message3: %1 temporarily cannot be killed.
message4: %1 is mortal again.
name: Immortal
description:
Being immortal is a special, temporary
effect, usually from some sort of magic,
which temporarily allows a character to
not drop over dead when their Health
Points reach zero and instead keep on
fighting.  While in effect it also
partially reduces all damage taken.  It
wears off when the battle is over, and it
also has a small chance to bork and wear
off early every time the affected
character is successfully hit by an
enemy's attack in combat.

message1: %1 is poisoned!
message2: %1 is poisoned!
message3: %1 is poisoned!
message4: %1 is no longer poisoned!
name: Poison
description:
A poisoned character loses HP (Health
Points) every turn in combat, as well as
every so many steps as the party walks
around on the map screen, anywhere the
adventuring party travels.  Until the
poison is cured, HP will drop at a
percent rate dependant upon the strength
of the poison, which cannot kill the
affected character while walking around
on the map screen, but will keep them
from having more than 1 single HP.
Healing spells and potions will provide
only temporary relief if the poison
continues to affect the character, as
their HP will continue to drop until it
reaches 1 HP again.\LB
    During combat, poison reduces HP
every combat turn for as long as the
character is poisoned, and can end up
making the character defeated and no
longer able to fight, if their HP drops
below 1 HP.\LB
    Poison isn't cured with simple, basic
healing methods, although such healing
will restore HP from the damage done
while the character is poisoned as well
as after they are cured.  Certain magic
spells, mostly holy magic spells a Cleric
can cast, can cure poison, and certain
magic potions and cures meant for curing
poison can remove this effect from an
inflicted character.\LB
    Note that not all poisonous
infections the same, and poisons vary in
strength.  Some will make HP drop very
slowly, while others are very
fast-acting.

message1: %1 is blinded!
message2: %1 is blinded!
message3: %1 is blinded!
message4: %1 is no longer blinded!
name: Blind
description:
Being blind, in this case, isn't quite
the type of blindness where one has a
garbage can at the end of a row of potted
plants in their home, and when it comes
time to water the plants one by one, they
end up watering the garbage.
\LB    Being blind in this case is rather
abruptly finding that, in combat with a
monster or creature of some sort, one
suddenly has something get in their eyes,
and no matter how much of a perceptive
type of person they are to begin with,
they simply, literally cannot see.  In
some cases this means something flew
through the air, or some creature sprayed
some sort of fluid perhaps, which ended
up in one's eyes, or maybe their eyeballs
became injured.
\LB    When a character is blind, they
will of course suffer a number of ability
score penalties, mostly related to aiming
and dodging.  Making counterattacks
becomes difficult to impossible.

message1: %1's magic is suppressed!  %1 can't focus to use magic!
message2: %1's magic is suppressed!  %1 can't focus to use magic!
message3: %1's magic is suppressed!  %1 can't focus to use magic!
message4: %1's magic is no longer suppressed!
name: Suppressed Magic
description:
All living creatures of the ten worlds,
including humans, plants, animals,
insects, etc., including people's pet
dogs, cats, and other house pets, have
magic that is part of their nature and
generated by their living spirit, ever
since they migrated over to the ten
worlds from Earth many thousands of years
ago and the native aliens of the ten
worlds infused their living spirits with
magic, enchanting them, so that all such
life would be born with magical gifts
that would vary from individual to
individual.  While not everyone of the
ten worlds learns to practice magic or
take advantage of their gifts they are
born with, they all have such potential,
unlike their mundane ancient ancestors
who stayed behind on Earth.  Even animals
sometimes figure out how to channel and
make use of their magical sides, such as
a person's pet cat that learns to make
it's food dish levitate and spin around
on the kitchen tile floor, making noise
to draw the attention of their owner and
remind them that they are hungry.  Wild
animals also sometimes learn a few small
magical tricks as well, which vary.  On
occasion, some even learn magic to throw
fireballs at prey when they go hunting
other animals, etc., or to defend
themselves against predators.
\LB    With intelligent creatures, such
as people, the strength of one's magical
gifts that they are born with are tied
to their mind and intelligence.  This
does lead to an achilles heel of sorts,
in that if a person's mind is impaired in
a certain way, it interferes with their
magic-using abilities.
\LB    Magic suppression is a mental
condition which does this, as it is a
curse or effect placed upon or induced in
an individual which impairs and disrupts
their ability to cast or use magic.  When
a character has suppressed magic, they
cannot use any skills that fall under the
category of magic, both inside and
outside of combat.
\LB    Magic suppression is itself often
caused by a magic spell or magical effect
of some sort.  Some spellcasters have
spells in their spellbooks that do this,
and some creatures have it as a power or
ability.  An enchanted magical piece of
equipment that induces it in someone
isn't unheard of either.  All of the
natives of the ten worlds, which are,
arguably, space aliens to life from Earth
to begin with, known as The Architects,
who gave life from Earth magical natures
as they colonized the ten worlds, have
vast innate magical powers to begin with,
including the ability to kill what they
create, so to speak, and as such they
have the power to induce magic
suppression in any creature that is of
Earth-origin to begin with, as well as
magical creatures that later evolved from
Earth-origin life that didn't exist in
the world of planet Earth to begin with,
except perhaps in fantasy books, films,
and video games.
\LB    Note that equipped items that are
enchanted with their own magical powers,
such as a magic ring that grants special
magical skills, are usually not affected
by the character's magic being
suppressed, as the ring's powers are used
by the character triggering the ring's
own internal magic that is not of the
character themself.

message1: %1 is enraged and out of control!
message2: %1 is enraged and out of control!
message4: %1 is no longer enraged!
name: Rage
description:
A magically enraged character madly
attacks a random enemy, not thinking
sensibly or using any particular
strategy or tact.  When a player
character of the adventuring party is
cursed with this effect, unlike when
things are normal you will not be able to
choose what they do during their turn in
combat, and you will also not have
control over who they attack, either.
\LB    A rage effect wears off at the end
of combat, and also has a chance to wear
off early if an enraged character is hurt
by an attack, whether it is from an enemy
or from an ally who is attempting to
knock some sense into the character and
make them snap out of it.  Certain magic
spells and magic items can also cure the
enragement curse.
\LB    Because of one's uncontrollable
fury and anger, a character who is
magically enraged will swing melee
weapons a lot harder than they normally
would, yet be a bit reckless and less
controlled than normal as they do so.
Because of this, an enraged character
temporarily fights with an effective
strength score higher than what it truly
is, while their skill at aiming attacks
is temporarily reduced.

message1: %1 is confused!
message2: %1 is confused!
message4: %1 is no longer confused!
name: Confusion
description:
A character cursed with magical confusion
can't keep track of who is a friend and
who is a foe.  The confused character
will still fight in a battle, and will
randomly pick another character from
either side, lacking consistency, and
attack them.
\LB    You cannot control or choose
actions for a player character in the
adventuring party like you normally
would during combat, until the effect
wears off or is dispelled, or until the
battle is over which automatically ends
the confusion.  The confusion curse will
also end after a few turns go by, if the
battle continues on for more than a few
turns.
\LB    Certain curative spells and magic
items will remove this effect.  Confusion
can also end early if the affected
character is struck and hurt by any
attack, whether from an enemy or an ally
that attacks him or her, striking them
to make them snap out of it, so to speak.
The chance of confusion ending when
getting hurt isn't 100 percent however,
and a "roll of the dice" is made every
time they are injured.

message1: %1 is charmed!
message2: %1 is charmed!
message4: %1 is no longer charmed!
name: Charm
description:
In combat, a charmed character is
magically cursed in that they fight for
the enemy by attacking their allies,
confused with their magically blinded
mindset.  If the charmed character is a
player character in the adventuring
party, they will no longer be under your
control and you will not be able to
control their actions during combat,
including who they fight, until the
curse has ended.
\LB    A charm curse ends automatically
at the end of any battle.  Certain magic
spells and special magic items from the
party's shared inventory will cure a
charm curse affecting a character.  In
addition, if the affected character
suffers any damage during battle,
regardless of if it is from the
adventuring party or an enemy's attack,
it will stop the curse early.  This holds
true for enemies who are charmed as well.

message1: %1 falls asleep!
message2: %1 falls asleep!
message3: %1 is sleeping.
message4: %1 wakes up!
name: Sleep
description:
As if this effect supposedly needed a
description, sleeping in combat is
typically something induced by magic or
something like sleeping gas which,
obviously, makes a character fall asleep.
A sleeping character can't move, act, or
counterattack during battle, or
effectively defend themselves from any
attack or injury for as long as they are
asleep.  Sleeping characters are also
more likely to suffer critical hits when
hurt by anyone or anything that attacks
them and scores a hit.
\LB    Sleeping can be interrupted by
certain magic items and spells that can
wake up the character so that they can
fight again.  Sleeping characters also
wake up at the end of any battle.
Otherwise, sleep will only last for a few
combat turns anyways, before it wears off
and the character wakes up.  Finally,
being hit by any attack that does any
damage, whether from an ally or an enemy,
will wake up the character.

message1: %1 is paralyzed from poison and can barely move!
message2: %1 is paralyzed from poison and can barely move!
message3: %1 is paralyzed from poison and can barely move!
message4: %1 is no longer paralyzed from poison!
name: Paralysis, Poison
description:
A paralyzed character cannot move very
well, and is impaired to the point that
they can't attack, fight, cast spells, or
otherwise act during combat, but can
still walk around with the rest of the
adventuring party outside of battle.
Paralyzed characters have a reduced
chance of avoiding getting hit by an
enemy's attack, an increased chance of an
enemy's attack to do critical hits to
them, and a reduced chance to make a
successful counterattack when attacked by
an enemy.
\LB    Paralysis that is induced by
poison is often from some animal or
creature that has a poisonous sting,
bite, gas, or other attack of some kind.
Toxic venom can induce poison-based
paralysis, as well as inorganic chemicals
of certain types.  This typically
includes non-magical poisons either way.
\LB    Paralysis will not wear off on
it's own once it takes effect, and will
linger in a character's body after a
battle and into the next fight, although
certain curative spells and magic items
will remove paralysis, as well as resting
at an Inn.  It will otherwise remain in
effect indefinitely.

description:
A paralyzed character cannot move very
well, and is impaired to the point that
they can't attack, fight, cast spells, or
otherwise act during combat, but can
still walk around with the rest of the
adventuring party outside of battle.
Paralyzed characters have a reduced
chance of avoiding getting hit by an
enemy's attack, an increased chance of an
enemy's attack to do critical hits to
them, and a reduced chance to make a
successful counterattack when attacked by
an enemy.
\LB    Paralysis that is brought about by
magical means are often from an enemy's
magic spell or power of some kind, and
are often more or less considered a
magical curse.
\LB    Paralysis will not wear off on
it's own once it takes effect, and will
linger in a character's body after a
battle and into the next fight, although
certain curative spells and magic items
will remove paralysis, as well as resting
at an Inn.  It will otherwise remain in
effect indefinitely.

message1: %1 is stunned and can't act!
message2: %1 is stunned and can't act!
message3: %1 is stunned and can't act!
message4: %1 is no longer stunned!
name: Stun
description:
When a character is considered to be
stunned, they have the wind knocked out
of themself, so to speak, for a turn or
two, and although they cannot act during
the turn that they are affected, being
stunned isn't anywhere near as severe as
paralysis or magical sleep.  Being
stunned is a physical condition, and not
usually from anything magical going on,
curse or otherwise.  It is often brought
about by being hit by a hard blow of a
melee weapon or other physical attack of
some sort, although certain spells that
do direct damage and are very powerful
may sometimes bring about this effect as
well.
\LB    Not too many spells or items will
undo or negate being stunned, but
fortunately the effect is normally very
short lived, and will often be over at
the end of the combat turn or the next
combat turn.  Whatever the case may be,
being stunned also wears off at the end
of battle if it is still in effect by
then.

name: None
description:
This character isn't currently subject to
any effects from anything, including
curses, magical effects, poisons, or any
other special conditions, beneficial
or harmful.\LB
    This can change when
certain spells are cast on this
individual, or if they are attacked by
something that has a lasting effect of
some kind, such as poison, infection,
acid burns, etc., and much more.

message1: %1 is melting from an acid burn!
message2: %1 is melting from an acid burn!
message3: %1 is melting from an acid burn!
message4: %1 is no longer melting!
name: Acid Burn
description:
Being affected by an acid burn means that
a character has been exposed to acid of
some kind that is eating away at their
flesh.\LB
    In combat, for every turn that goes
by the character will suffer a loss of a
certain number of HP (Health Points).
This will continue until the acid wears
off and stops working, or until the
character is defeated when their HP
reaches zero.\LB
    On the map screen, a character with
an acid burn will lose HP every so often
as the adventuring party walks a certain
number of spaces in any direction.  If the
character suffering from the acid burn
loses all of their HP, they will end up
with 1 HP left and no lower, and any
damage healed from basic healing methods
will bring only temporary relief as the
acid will continue to do more damage.\LB
    Acid burns are not cured or stopped by
regular healing methods that simply heal
HP.  An acid neutralizer magic potion will
stop acid damage immediately and take away
the acid burn effect.  Certain holy magic
spells that a Cleric can cast may also
negate or stop acid burns and prevent
further damage.  Note that stopping an
acid burn typically still leaves the
character in an injured state.

message1: %1 is cursed with Brain Fog!
message2: %1 is cursed with Brain Fog!
message3: %1 is still cursed with Brain Fog!
message4: %1 is no longer cursed with Brain Fog!
name: Brain Fog
description:
Brain Fog is a name for a very unpleasant
curse.  It is a state of fogged-up and
cloudy thinking, where clear and lucid,
sharp thoughts are difficult to
impossible, and where one is something of
a "space cadet," where they don't have
the ability to pay attention to or focus
upon things, no matter how hard they try.
\LB    It also brings about a very nasty
and unpleasant non-stop sensation, one
that is something like what getting a
lack of sleep every night brings about,
except that it isn't quite the same as
drowsiness or sleepiness, and if an
affected character tries to sleep it off
or reduce it with rest, it doesn't ever
go away.  The sensation it brings about
sometimes also feels like eating could
possibly help, but food does not make
brain fog go away or diminish.  Brain fog
is torture in how it always feels like
such things would cure or diminish it,
but don't.  The way in which it teases
and tantalizes, bringing about such
frustration, is inhumane.

message1: %1 is cursed with Mind Fire!
message2: %1 is cursed with Mind Fire!
message3: %1 is still cursed with Mind Fire!
message4: %1 is no longer cursed with Mind Fire!
name: Mind Fire
description:
Mind Fire is a state of
non-stop perpetual pain and agony of the
mind, and while not necessarily being a
headache, is an extreme mentally
stressful sensation that is overbearing
and can easily lead to distress and even
panic.  Needless to say, it is easily
described as torture.\LB
    Mind Fire is not alleviated by food,
rest, or relaxation of any sort, but has
a deceptive nature to it that brings
about an illusion that eating or relaxing
might supposedly bring relief.  In this
way it tantalizes one who suffers from
it, in ways that are inhumane, while also
difficult to put into words.
\LB    Mind Fire is very debilitating,
painful agony in it's own way, and is a
curse of sorts induced by mundane or
magical means.  It is inhumane, and as
such only evil characters and other
beings will have abilities, spells, or
skills that cause it.

message1: %1 is effected by an arcane rune's power!
message2: %1 is effected by an arcane rune's power!
message3: %1 is effected by an arcane rune's power!
message4: %1 is no longer effected by an arcane rune's power.
name: Rune Effect, Adamantine
description:
(Arcane Rune) When equipped, this rune
makes a character tougher and less
breakable, less easily injured, able to
take more damage while suffering less
than usual from various types of mundane
and magical damage and attacks, and less
prone to being weakened or debilitated by
a number of different things.  It also
makes incoming attacks do fewer critical
hits.  Incoming attacks that stun,
poison, and debuff certain ability scores
will be less likely to successfully work.
description2:
Arcane runes are very special magic
accessories that provide various
protections and/or enhancements to a
character that has the rune equipped.
Only one rune or accessory can be
equipped at a time.\LB
    Runes can be overcharged.  When a
rune is overcharged in the midst of
combat, the effects will last until the
battle is over.  If a rune is
overcharged outside of combat on the
Skills screen, this places an effect on
one or more characters ahead of a battle,
which then expire at the end of the next
battle.  There are two ways a rune can be
overcharged, one which affects only the
owner of the rune if it is equipped, and
the other method which affects the entire
party.  Using the rune on only themself
creates a more potent effect.  Note that
using the rune on the whole party counts
as multiple uses towards the limit of
however many times the rune may be used
before it breaks.\LB
    Runes are worth a good amount of
money, and most merchants will pay a
decent amount for an unwanted rune.  Most
merchants will however not offer runes
for sale in their shops, as arcane runes
are rather rare and hard to come by.\LB
    Runes are designed and crafted by the
natives of the ten magical worlds, known
as The Architects, who made such
artifacts before the coming of humans and
other Earth-origin life from planet Earth
thousands of years ago before your
adventure started.  Runes were around
before the ten worlds became terraformed
to accept people and other life of Earth,
and after such Earth-origin life moved in
and settled in the ten worlds, and became
enchanted by the natives to have magic
generated by their living spirits, such
life of the world of planet Earth found
that their new magical natures were
compatible with the magic of arcane
runes, among other things, while still
retaining the mundane sides of themselves
which flourished and thrived in the ten
worlds thanks to the skills and
accomplishments of The Architects that
welcomed this life from Earth.

name: Panicked
description:
A character who has panicked is terribly
frightened, frozen still in place, and
unable to think clearly or bring themself
to act during their turn in combat.  While
cowering in fear and shock, they are
incapable of defending themselves
effectively from enemy attack, and are
easy targets that can't dodge or block
anything.\LB
    Becoming panicked is usually something
that happens when an intimidating monster
or creature scares the affected character,
whether from size or something else, such
as a loud roar or yell a monster may make.
In rare cases, a hostile creature may have
some sort of magical or psychic special
power, or a magic spell or ability that
can induce quick yet intense fear in
another.\LB
    Panicked characters are more vulnerable
to becoming affected by new effects,
curses, debuffs, and more, from special
attacks that enemies sometimes have.\LB
    During combat there is little that
can be done about a scared character,
other than to wait for the character to
come to their senses and be able to
control themself enough that they can act
again.  Fortunately, their fright is
typically short-lived and over with in
only a turn or two.\LB
    Characters with a specific genetic
gift that allows them many benefits are
usually rather brave, and as such are
resistant to becoming scared.  Certain
characters are also tougher or more brave
than other characters by nature, and as
such are simply more or less panic-prone
due to their personality or species, etc.
Many opponents of the adventuring party
that the party gets attacked by in
wilderness areas include wild animals,
and the smaller wild animals in
particular can startle and become scared
more easily, but it varies.

name: Magic Flower Enchantment
description:
(Magic Item) A Magic Flower will
bestow a magical enchantment upon one
individual, which lasts for a limited
amount of time.  The flower is consumed
in the process.  The enchantment offers
enhancements to ability scores and
partial protection from
ability-score-lowering debuffs.
description2:
Magic flowers have distant ancestry
that goes back thousands of years to
planet Earth, and very far back are
relatives of flowering plant species
native to Earth, which were brought to
Acrydia and nine other worlds by the
ancient natives of the ten worlds that
brought in life from Earth and
terraformed their ten worlds into being
like that of Earth, although with the
imported Earth-origin life being gifted
with magic that became natural to the
spirit of all such life, resulting in
plants, animals, and people from Earth
having magical gifts that would vary from
individual to individual.\LB
    Magic flowers are of course an
example of such enchanted life, a
non-sentient plant species that has a
highly magical nature that is tied to
the spirit of the plant.  Such flowers
grow in the wilderness as well as magic
gardens of people of the ten magical
worlds, and are edible plants that can
be safely eaten raw for nutrition and
magical benefits, as well as being used
as an ingredient in both foods and
magic potions, oils, bread, and other
magical and herbal products that include
various foods and medicines.\LB
    Once they are picked from the plant
that bears them, magic flowers will last
a suprisingly long time before they
start to go bad and decay if they are not
consumed.  On the other hand, there isn't
any reliable method of preserving them to
make them last longer, although the
flowers themselves can be preservatives
for other perishable foods and products,
which is why breads and pastries baked
with magic flowers as an ingredient last
a rather long time before going stale.
